sources.title: Crop Mapping in Palestine for Winter and Spring Seasons 2023–24
sources.organization: Applied Research Institute–Jerusalem, Food and Agriculture Organization, Palestinian Ministry of Agriculture, and Palestinian Water Authority
sources.temporal_coverage: Jericho winter 2023–2024 and spring 2024 crop mapping and field surveys.
sources.methodology: ARIJ, FAO, the agriculture ministry and water authority used Sentinel-2 imagery, field surveys and 366 ground-truth points.
sources.limitations: The page intro refers to 2025 mapping, unlike its title and detailed 2023–2024 survey dates; findings are Jericho-specific.

sources.title: Humanitarian Situation Update #314: West Bank
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, occupied Palestinian territory
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian and water-access conditions reported through 14 August 2025, with some water analysis from early 2025.
sources.methodology: OCHA situation update drawing on WASH Cluster analysis, partner reporting and documented incidents.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting is time-bounded; water-shortage drivers and access varied by community.

sources.title: Enhancing Adaptation Planning and Adoption of Climate Resilient Agriculture in Palestine
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Project page lists a period from 25 August 2020 through 24 August 2025.
sources.methodology: FAO project summary describing the proposal's objective, partners, budget and stated dates.
sources.limitations: Page states planned objectives but does not document implementation or outcomes.

claims.locator: Main findings, climate and environmental challenges; page lines 145–151.
claims.paraphrase: For Jericho, FAO reports January–July 2024 temperatures 1.5–3°C above historical averages, shortening crop growth periods; 2023 evaporation was 371.3 mm above average.
claims.limitations: These are reported local observations, not a forward projection or national average.

claims.locator: Main findings, 'Who farms where'; page lines 131–144.
claims.paraphrase: The Jericho mapping says Palestinian farmers had limited water access constraining crop choices, while Israeli settlers had greater water and technology access.
claims.limitations: The reported access contrast is for the mapped Jericho area, not all farmers or all settlements.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO identifies occupation-related land and water restrictions as a major farming constraint.

claims.locator: Introduction and study objectives; page lines 24–32.
claims.paraphrase: Movement and transport restrictions linked to the security situation constrained field access and sampling; ARIJ adapted sampling and used satellite analysis to validate and extend observations.
claims.limitations: This is an access constraint on the crop-mapping exercise, not a measured limit on farm adaptation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The study explicitly attributes survey-access limits to movement restrictions and the security situation.

claims.locator: Key highlights and Water Sanitation and Hygiene Cluster analysis; webpage paragraphs dated 14 August 2025.
claims.paraphrase: OCHA reports heatwaves and low rainfall alongside pipeline reductions, permit limits, infrastructure demolitions and settler violence in West Bank water shortages; 52 communities faced access obstacles and 73 relied on trucking without official networks.
claims.limitations: Community counts are from WASH Cluster analysis at the beginning of 2025, not a current 2026 estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: OCHA attributes shortages to weather as well as restrictions, demolition and settler violence.

claims.locator: Umm al Kheir incident; webpage paragraph dated 5 August 2025.
claims.paraphrase: After settlers repeatedly disconnected Umm al Kheir's main water line, 200 residents, including 108 children, lacked running water and relied on water trucking.
claims.limitations: The situation update describes a dated incident; it does not report later restoration status.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Settler attacks interrupted the community's local water connection.

claims.locator: Water response in Umm al Kheir and other communities; webpage paragraph dated 14 August 2025.
claims.paraphrase: The WASH Cluster and Palestinian Water Authority used water trucking, mobile tanks and maintenance kits, which partly alleviated shortages, while communities continued requesting water.
claims.limitations: OCHA reports partial relief and continued unmet requests, not an evaluated resilience outcome.

claims.locator: Project objective and stated period; webpage lines 21–34.
claims.paraphrase: FAO's 2020–2025 project proposed stronger climate-resilient agriculture coordination, real-time agro-weather information for smallholders and two test plots with farmer associations.
claims.limitations: These are proposal objectives for a period ending in 2025; the page does not establish implementation or completion.

access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.notes: Published 14 August 2025; retained as a dated operational record, not a current 2026 estimate.

search_audit.outcome: Opened FAO's Jericho crop mapping and OCHA's West Bank situation update; both contain directly read named-area climate/water findings.

search_audit.outcome: OCHA explicitly reports heat and low rainfall together with restrictions, demolitions and settler violence as drivers of water shortages; FAO reports occupation-related resource constraints on Jericho farmers.

search_audit.outcome: The OCHA page directly documents settler attacks severing Umm al Kheir's water connection; the FAO crop-mapping team reports movement/security constraints on field access.

search_audit.outcome: FAO's project page states planned agro-weather and climate-resilient agriculture capacity objectives; OCHA reports the actual but partial emergency water response in named communities.

gaps: The inspected OCHA report provides a direct joint climate/access pathway for West Bank water stress but does not establish climate-caused violence.
FAO crop-mapping findings are limited to Jericho and 2023–2024; its page contains inconsistent survey-year and temperature statements, which are noted and not reconciled.
The GCF 2024 performance report and UN Country Results Report PDF returned HTTP 403; claims from their search-result text were excluded.
FAO's agriculture adaptation project page states objectives and dates but not evaluated delivery; no implementation outcomes are inferred.
